**THE v2 SHELL IMPLEMENTATION IS DELETED AT THE CUT, FAIL-FORWARD -- AND THAT IS 26 FILES, NOT THE `bin/` DIRECTORY.** POPULATION A, THE SUBJECT: `bin/intent` + 25 `bin/intent_*`. POPULATION B, WHICH MUST SURVIVE: `bin/int`, `bin/devbin`, `bin/.devbin/` -- v3's own build and delivery system, and `bin/devbin build all` is the ONLY door that produces a coherent binary pair. **A criterion whose plain reading deletes the release system is not a stricter criterion, it is a wrong one.**

**THE `bin/` COUPLING IS DISCHARGED (cc, 92817292, 2026-09-05) AND THE COUNT IS DERIVED HERE RATHER THAN TRANSCRIBED, BECAUSE THIS ROW'S PREVIOUS COUNT ROTTED IN SIX DAYS AND MADE THE WORK LOOK FOUR TIMES BIGGER THAN IT WAS.** It read *blocked on four call sites, all in one file* and named `:67` HELPERS, `:373` doctor, `:663` agents sync, `:690` claude upgrade. Three had already been ported and the script's own comment at `:81` recorded it; **and the survivor was not a call site but a `source`, pulling a 700-line file in for exactly ONE symbol.** A two-edge sweep of all 57 population-B files against the full 38-symbol roster returned ONE edge: `release -> stamp_project_version`, ported verbatim because its caller reads `$?` as a three-way. The other apparent matches were the English word *error* in comments and `require_intent_bin`, which `release:128` defines locally and always did -- **the row's count was matching the script's own function.** REGENERATE, do not read a number off this row: sweep population B for `bin/<name>` at a word boundary, excluding comment lines.

**THREE BINDINGS LIVE OUTSIDE `bin/` AND THE FOUR-SITE LIST NEVER COUNTED THEM, WHICH IS WHY THE DELETION IS NOT A SWEEP EVEN NOW.** (i) **20 BATS files whose only subject is population A** -- 33 of 116 reference it, 13 of those also touch v3. (ii) **A LIVE SHIPPED CITATION IN RUST**: `legacy.rs:49` holds `WP_TEMPLATE_SUBST = "bin/intent_wp:113"`, interpolated at `:1210` into an emitted disposition reason a user reads -- **and it is a POSITION citation, which is the exact class AC-00.10 retracts at length. Deleting population A turns a shipped sentence into a reference to nothing.** (iii) The `surface/dispatch-table` and `MODULES.md` rows.

**AND THIS ROW'S COVERING INSTRUMENT CANNOT SEE ITS SUBJECT.** `tests/cutover_guard.bash` asks the right question with a two-edge method and a control arm, and `:58-59` declares its population as four directories -- `intent/plugins/claude/bin`, `intent/plugins/claude/lib`, `lib/templates/hooks`, `lib/templates/.claude/scripts`. **`.devbin` appears in it ZERO times.** So it printed `ok: 16 file(s) surviving the prune, none depending on bin/` throughout the entire period the release script sourced `intent_helpers` outright. **ITS GREEN WAS NEVER ABOUT THE ONE FILE THIS CRITERION IS ABOUT.** The instrument is not careless -- `:66` dies if the population is EMPTY -- **and that is the distinction worth carrying: it guards against measuring nothing and does not guard against measuring the wrong thing, so a non-empty wrong population passes the guard and reads as coverage.**

**WHAT WOULD FALSIFY THIS:** any population-A file surviving the cut; any population-B file deleted with it; a release path that still executes population A; or a shipped artefact still citing a population-A path after the deletion. **THE DELETION ITSELF IS AT THE CUT, per this row's own wording, and is not owed before the tag. What was owed before the tag was the coupling, and it is gone.**
